findings.statement: CXCR2 tops the convergence ranking: pooled UC-vs-control change is up in all eight cohorts [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.838], and in the same patients inflamed mucosa is higher than non-inflamed [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]. Non-inflamed mucosa shows only a small rise, so this is mainly a local-inflammation signal. As a neutrophil receptor, the bulk rise probably reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than a change inside the tissue (interpretation, to be confirmed by the cell-context specialist).

CXCL8 (IL-8) is strongly and reproducibly up in UC across all eight cohorts [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687]. The change in MSCCR inflamed mucosa holds after adjustment for colon segment, age and sex [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=2.499]. Together with CXCR2 and CXCR1 this suggests a neutrophil chemokine axis; part of the bulk signal may come from infiltrating myeloid cells (interpretation).

IDO1 is up in inflamed mucosa versus non-inflamed mucosa of the same patient [gene=IDO1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6828]. Non-inflamed mucosa is only modestly raised against control [gene=IDO1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.535], so it marks local inflammation.

CHI3L1 is among the largest pooled increases and is up in all eight cohorts [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.913]. At protein level the direction replicates but the effect is far smaller [gene=CHI3L1; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=0.607], and the proteomics authors did not call it significant. The RNA size should therefore not be read as a protein-level effect size.

S100A8 is significantly up in all eight cohorts in the pooled analysis and replicates strongly as protein in independent UC mucosa [gene=S100A8; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=2.749], significant by the authors.

DUOX2 is significantly up in all eight cohorts in the pooled analysis, and the MSCCR inflamed change holds after adjusting for segment, age and sex [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=3.263].

HMGCS2 is significantly down in all eight cohorts in the pooled analysis, and the loss is also seen as protein [gene=HMGCS2; type=proteomics_de; source=DATASET:PROTEOMICS_SCHNIERS2019; contrast=inflamed UC at diagnosis vs healthy colon mucosa; log2_ratio=-3.094]. A lost gene of this kind would suit a biomarker rather than a target (interpretation).

AQP8 shows the largest pooled decrease in the top-gene list, down in all eight cohorts, and the MSCCR loss holds after adjustment [gene=AQP8; type=expression_adjusted; source=DATASET:GSE193677; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed UC vs control, biopsy level; adjusted_log2fc=-3.78]. This suggests a biomarker of mucosal damage rather than a target (interpretation).

JAK2 has a small pooled increase [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.833] but it is significant and up in every one of the eight cohorts. It ranks highly because of genetics and tractability, not because of a large expression change. The small size means expression alone does not single it out.
CD274 (PD-L1) is up in UC with a moderate pooled change [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.937], same direction in all eight cohorts.

caveats: Pooled log2FC values come from cohorts with very high heterogeneity (I2 about 0.9 for most top genes); compare direction and significance, not size, across microarray and RNA-seq cohorts.
Immune and chemokine genes (CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8, IDO1) may reflect infiltrating neutrophils and myeloid cells; composition adjustment and single-cell checks belong to the cell-context specialist.
Adjusted-change and paired inflamed-vs-non-inflamed analyses come from the MSCCR cohort only.
Protein replication is from a single small proteomics study; CHI3L1 protein was not called significant by its authors.
No drug, pathway, cell-source or protein-function claims are made because the matching records were not retrieved.
